meta.title: Frankencoin glossary
meta.description: Short definitions of ZCHF, FCS, svZCHF, positions, challenges, the savings rate and other Frankencoin terms.

hero.subtitle: Terms you will meet on this site and in the app.

terms.def: The Frankencoin token: a digital Swiss franc backed by on-chain collateral worth more than one franc.
Frankencoin Shares, the share and governance token: a claim on the reserve and a vote with veto rights.
Frankencoin Pool Shares, the earlier equity token. FCS wraps FPS one-to-one; new participants use FCS.
Savings Vault token: ZCHF deposited in the savings module, held as one token whose value grows with the savings rate.
The contract that pays the savings rate on ZCHF deposited into it. ZCHF in a wallet earns nothing by itself.
The yearly rate paid on ZCHF in the savings module. Set and changed through governance; also called the lead rate.
Your loan contract: it holds your collateral and records the ZCHF you minted, with terms fixed when you open it.
What you lock in a position to borrow against: BTC, ETH, tokenized gold or shares.
The collateral price below which your position can be challenged and the collateral auctioned. Keep a buffer above it.
How much you borrow relative to your collateral's market value. Lower is safer.
Interest for the whole term, deducted from the ZCHF you receive when you mint.
A share of what you mint that stays in the reserve and comes back when you repay.
A public claim that a position's collateral is worth less than its liquidation price. It starts an auction that settles the question.
ZCHF held by the protocol, funded by interest and FCS purchases. It pays the savings rate and covers shortfalls when an auction does not repay a debt; FCS is a claim on it.
The right of FCS holders with enough votes to block a proposed collateral or protocol change.
Chainlink's cross-chain protocol, used to move ZCHF between the chains it lives on. See [exchanges and wallets](/for/exchanges-wallets).
ZCHF trading at one Swiss franc. Held by over-collateralization and arbitrage, not by issuer redemption.
